title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: AWS
providers.scope_notes: Covers Amazon Web Services (IAM, STS, IAM Identity Center, IAM Roles Anywhere, Amazon Bedrock). All features are available in every AWS account; SCPs and centralized root access require AWS Organizations, and Control Tower controls require AWS Control Tower.

controls.name: Deactivate / delete access key (UpdateAccessKey, DeleteAccessKey)
controls.what: Setting a key Inactive or deleting it stops all further use of that key.
controls.setting: IAM console > Users > Security credentials > Actions > Deactivate/Delete; API UpdateAccessKey / DeleteAccessKey

controls.name: AWS-GR_RESTRICT_ROOT_USER_ACCESS_KEYS
controls.what: Control Tower preventive control (SCP) that denies iam:CreateAccessKey for the root principal.

controls.name: Root access management (Root credentials management)
controls.what: Lets the management account or delegated admin delete member-account root passwords, access keys and certificates; new accounts get no root credentials.
controls.setting: IAM console > Root access management > Enable

controls.name: aws:SourceIp deny policy
controls.what: Identity policy or SCP that denies any request from outside listed CIDR ranges.
controls.setting: IAM policy / SCP with NotIpAddress aws:SourceIp

no_control.what: IAM policies cannot restrict the root user's permissions.

controls_unknown: Whether long-term Bedrock API keys can be set to never expire, and their maximum lifetime.
Token format/prefix for Bedrock API keys (not documented on fetched pages).
Which CloudTrail field identifies the specific Bedrock API key on a request (key value is not logged).
Default session duration for IAM Roles Anywhere when durationSeconds is omitted.
Exact CloudTrail eventName strings for CreateAccessKey/UpdateAccessKey/DeleteAccessKey were not shown on fetched pages (they match the IAM API action names, which CloudTrail logs).

authentication.summary: Access key pair for the AWS account root user; signs API calls with full, unrestrictable account access.

federation.details: Root keys are tied to the account root user, not to any IdP. Docs do not discuss IdP policy for them.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only via an SCP on member accounts with aws:SourceIp. IAM identity policies cannot be attached to the root user, and SCPs do not affect the management account.

renewal.summary: Reused until deleted; up to two keys.

administration.summary: Only the root user can create its keys. With centralized root access (AWS Organizations), the management account or delegated admin can delete member-account root keys, and new accounts start without root credentials. Control Tower provides an SCP denying root iam:CreateAccessKey.
administration.conditions: Requires AWS Organizations; centralized root access must be enabled.

sso.details: AWS says root user access keys cannot be used with MFA-protected API access.

inventory.details: The IAM credential report includes the root user and access key status for each account.

inventory.ui: IAM console > Credential report > Download Report
inventory.cli: aws iam generate-credential-report; aws iam get-credential-report

network.ui: AWS Organizations console > Policies > Service control policies > Create policy (Deny * with NotIpAddress aws:SourceIp) > attach to OU/account (member accounts only)
network.cli: aws organizations create-policy --type SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY; aws organizations attach-policy

reads.ui: CloudTrail console > Trails > trail > Data events > Edit > enable S3 data events; then filter trail logs on eventName=GetObject (not in Event history)

token_format.notes: Same AKIA format as IAM user keys.

log_sources.name: AWS CloudTrail event history
log_sources.notes: On by default; 90 days of management events per Region; free. Data events (e.g. S3 GetObject) not included.

log_sources.name: CloudTrail trail / event data store
log_sources.notes: Needed for retention beyond 90 days; data events off by default and cost extra.

credential_id_fields.notes: Key ID used to sign the request; may be empty for security reasons.

anomaly_cues: Root key creation in a member account

containment.steps: Delete the key as root, or from the management account via centralized root access management.
containment.notes: Root permissions cannot be scoped down by IAM policy, so deletion is the only fix.

unknown: Whether temporary credentials created by root via GetSessionToken survive key deletion.

calls.log_notes: All STS calls logged as management events; cannot be denied by policy.

calls.reveals: All IAM users, groups, roles, policies
All buckets owned by the account
calls.log_notes: Management/data classification not verified on fetched pages.
S3 object-level data event; only logged if data events are enabled on a trail (extra cost).

detections.title: PUA - AWS TruffleHog Execution
detections.detects: Any CloudTrail event with the TruffleHog user agent.

detections.title: Root Account Activity
detections.detects: Write actions by the root user (console or root access key), excluding service-invoked events.

detections.title: AWS Root Credentials
detections.detects: Any root user activity that is not an AWS service event.
